Thanks for the intro call earlier. Procurement asked me to share the token profile and a rough run-rate so we can get an indicative Dedicated commitment and expected latency SLA. Attaching the CSV with our 30-day production token histogram (peak windows highlighted). High level context:
- Product: in-app assistant + document extraction; typical response size ~32 tokens (generation) + ~8 tokens for system ops = ~40 tokens per request.
- Expected steady-state: ~1.6M tokens/day. Peak windows: two 45-minute spikes daily driven by batch user jobs.
- Desired SLO: p95 generation latency <= 600ms.

Can you sketch an initial tokens/sec to GPU mapping and recommended headroom for a committed Dedicated slab? Need something we can show our finance and infra teams this week.

Grace / Ben / Marissa — quick sizing sketch and assumptions. I ran a three-scenario capacity simulation based on the attached token histogram. Attachments: pioneer_capacity_slate_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — contains the calc workbook. Highlights below: 

Assumptions (call these out when we send to Pioneer):
- Model baseline: rw-7B-8bit (production profile we recommend for Pioneer workload); fallback: rw-3B-quant for heavy burst degradation.
- Request token mix: median response 32 tokens, +8 system = 40 tokens/request. Average tokens/request used in calc = 40.
- Effective per-GPU throughput (observed on our A100/80GB-equivalent nodes with steady batching and KV caching warm):
  - rw-7B-8bit: ~800 tokens/sec per GPU (p95-friendly tuning, concurrency ~40 requests/GPU)
  - rw-3B-quant: ~1,500 tokens/sec per GPU (used as fallback or cost-optimized variant)
- Batching and KV cache: we assume 20% effective gain during steady windows; spikes get reduced gains (5-10%).

Scenarios (peak window engineering):
1) Conservative commit (recommended):
   - Peak concurrency observed in CSV: 120 requests at peak  (Pioneer measurement after parsing).
   - Tokens/sec peak = 120 reqs * 40 tokens = 4,800 tokens/sec.
   - GPUs required at rw-7B (~800 t/s each) = 6.0 -> round up to 7 GPUs to meet p95 < 600ms and to provide room for small microbursts.
   - Suggested safety buffer: +20% (operational headroom) => provision 8 GPUs for committed slab.
   - Notes: With 8 GPUs, sustained peak fits and p95 projected ~450ms in our internal sims. If a heavier median or longer seq occurs, p95 could drift up — we call that out.
2) Cost-optimized commit (hybrid):
   - Provision 5 GPUs dedicated at rw-7B and 2 GPUs configured for rw-3B-quant as fast-fallback/burst pool.
   - Effective combined capacity ~5*800 + 2*1500 = 4,000 + 3,000 = 7,000 t/s of burst-handling capacity, but with graceful degradation on quality.
   - Expected p95 during normal peaks: ~520ms; during extreme, fallback shifts some load to rw-3B with slight quality delta.
3) Minimal commit (pilot):
   - 3 GPUs dedicated rw-7B + managed hosted burst for heavy spikes.
   - Risk: frequent fallback to hosted burst (higher cost, potential cold-start) and p95 violation risk during sustained peaks.

Operational recommendations:
- Canary + autoscaling policy: allow a 2-node burst pool for short, verified bursts beyond committed slab (2–10 minute windows).
- KV prefix caching: Pioneer should pin common prompts and doc prefixes (we can help with a small prompt-set audit). Caching reduces tokens served from model by ~8-12% in our tests.
- Quantization: Offer rw-3B-quant as a documented fallback route in the SLA doc; include quality delta examples.
- Monitoring & alerting: set token-level alert at 70% of committed slab, automatic paging at 90% sustained for 5+ minutes.

Attachments: pioneer_capacity_slate_v1.xlsx — sheet 'Scenarios' has the calc and per-minute trace. I also exported the CSV into the workbook for reproducibility.

If you want, I can prepare a short one-page summary (PDF) we can send to Samir + procurement that lists the recommended commit (8 GPUs) and the hybrid option.

- Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pioneer Labs initial capacity ask — tokens/sec profile attached

Samir — thanks for the token profile. Priyom and I discussed options and attached a short summary for procurement (pioneer_proposal_summary.pdf). TL;DR recommendation and next steps below.

Recommendation (what to sign):
- Committed Dedicated slab: 8 GPUs (A100/80GB-equivalent) running rw-7B-8bit. Rationale: matches projected peak (4.8k t/s) with a 20% operational buffer. Expected p95 generation latency ~450ms under the modeled peak.

Hybrid alternative (if Pioneer wants lower monthly commit):
- 5 GPUs dedicated rw-7B + 2 GPUs configured as rw-3B-quant burst pool. This lowers commit but requires documented fallback quality expectations.

Operational notes / SLO items to include in agreement:
- Token-level alerting thresholds: 70% and 90% with automated escalation.
- Short burst pool (2 nodes) available for 2–10 minute microbursts; longer bursts will be handled by the hybrid fallback or hosted overflow (per second pricing).
- Quarterly review of token patterns and a clause to re-size the slab after two consecutive months of sustained higher peaks.

Attachments included: pioneer_capacity_slate_v1.xlsx, pioneer_proposal_summary.pdf (one-page SLA + pricing sketch). Also included the CSV Pioneer provided for traceability.

Next steps: 
1) If this looks good, procurement can review the summary PDF and we can lock the deal_id PL-2026-037 into a term sheet.
2) Engineering (Priyom) will schedule a quick runbook walkthrough with Pioneer infra for KV prefix recommendations.
3) We will add a 30-day monitoring window post-go-live where we provide weekly token-latency heatmaps.

Samir — happy to hop on a 30-minute call with your finance/procurement this week to walk through the numbers. 

Best,
